hypotheses.binder: (hprim : Ideal.span (Set.range (fun index : Fin (n + 1) →₀ ℕ => coeff index (f : MvPowerSeries (Fin (n + 1)) V))) = ⊤)
hypotheses.justification: `hprim` follows from `htop` and `hc`. By `htop` and `hc`, the coefficient `(finSuccEquiv _ n (restrictedResidue a ham f)).coeff d = C c` is nonzero. So `finSuccEquiv _ n (restrictedResidue a ham f) ≠ 0`, and since `finSuccEquiv` is an algebra equivalence, `restrictedResidue a ham f ≠ 0`. Hence some index has `(restrictedResidue a ham f).coeff index ≠ 0`. By `coeff_restrictedResidue` (LeadingTerm.lean), that coefficient equals `Ideal.Quotient.mk (maximalIdeal V) (coeff index f)`. Since it is nonzero, `coeff index f ∉ maximalIdeal V` (by `Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem`), so it is a unit by `IsLocalRing.notMem_maximalIdeal`. It lies in the span of the range (`Ideal.subset_span`), so `Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem` gives span = ⊤. To prove the theorem without `hprim`, first derive it this way, then run the existing proof unchanged. No degenerate case is excluded: the argument only needs `c ≠ 0`. Note that `hprim` and `hc` can each be deleted on their own, but not both together.

`hc` follows from `hprim`, `hdegree` and `htop`. Suppose `c = 0`. Then `htop` says `p.coeff d = 0` for `p := finSuccEquiv _ n (restrictedResidue a ham f)`, and `hdegree` says `d = p.natDegree`. So `p.leadingCoeff = 0`, hence `p = 0` (`Polynomial.leadingCoeff_eq_zero`), hence `restrictedResidue a ham f = 0` because `finSuccEquiv` is an equivalence. By `coeff_restrictedResidue`, every `coeff index f` then maps to 0 in `V ⧸ maximalIdeal V`, i.e. every `coeff index f` lies in `maximalIdeal V`. Then `Ideal.span_le` gives span ≤ maximalIdeal V ≠ ⊤, which contradicts `hprim`. So `c ≠ 0` can be proved by contradiction and the existing proof then applies. `hc` and `hprim` can each be deleted on their own, but not both together.
